name: meter
title: Meter
description: A measurement within a known range.
use: Where a quantity stands in a range: storage used, a score, a password's strength. The element's low, high and optimum attributes decide the tone, so no class picks the color: ink while the value is where it should be, the warning ink when it is off, the danger ink when it is far off. A meter does not print its number: write the reading beside it, in words that say what the color says.

instead.when: It is how far a task has come, or the amount is unknown; a meter has no indeterminate state
The figure itself is the message, with what it measures and how it moved

platform.feature: Styling the parts of the native meter (Chromium and Firefox)
platform.fallback: Safari keeps the platform's own meter, which reports the same value and the same three tones in its own style

classes.name: meter
classes.description: A native meter element with a label: a 6px well with a fill whose tone follows low, high and optimum. The text inside the element is a fallback

classes.name: meter-segmented
classes.description: The track in --meter-steps equal pieces, four by default, for a reading that comes in levels

properties.name: --meter-steps
properties.description: Number of pieces of a segmented track; set it to the number of levels

example:
<label class="field">
  7.4 of 10 GB used, getting full
  <meter class="meter" min="0" max="10" low="6" high="9" optimum="0" value="7.4">7.4 of 10 GB</meter>
</label>
